why: The same list, executed by both implementations, for the four engines that
make up one mind: affect, relationship, reputation-and-identity, memory.
Chosen for where a port goes wrong rather than for coverage. Three themes
ORDER. Python dicts and lists keep insertion order, and this runtime sums
floating point over them -- so a different order is a different last bit,
not a different layout. `appraise` returns emotions in first-appearance
order; relationship deltas are grouped in arrival order and summed; the
identity softmax normalises over an ordered map.
STABILITY. Python sorts are stable and std::sort is not. On a tie, memory
retrieval picks which memory a character brings up and consolidation picks
TRUTHINESS. `if appraisal.get('prior_fear')` is not a presence test: a
prior fear of exactly 0.0 fires nothing, and a port that checks for the key

contracts.why: Every constant that exists precisely so two places cannot disagree -- the layer list, what each layer needs under it, the fields nothing writes, the runtime version, the player id, and every config default. A port is one more copy of all of them, and a copy drifts. Compared word for word, because a layer description that says something different in C++ is a lie in a /capabilities response.

roundtrip.why: as_dict then from_dict then as_dict again. Only the primitives round-trip -- expected_prob, ignorance and conflict are recomputed -- so this is the check that a restored save resumes the session it came from rather than a similar one.

A record with no origin_counts, which is what an older save looks like. The index is rebuilt from provenance -- otherwise loading a save quietly turns a saturated rumour back into fresh evidence, and the character becomes certain of something they had stopped believing.
Every field that influences future activation must round-trip, or a restored save drifts from the session it was taken from. presentations especially: they ARE the activation.
Mood, baseline and every targeted emotion. Full precision on purpose -- rounding the persistence shape is what makes a round-trip lossy.

predicates.why: A world pack declares predicates its story needs. Registering the same shape twice is fine; registering a DIFFERENT shape must raise, because slot order determines the canonical core key and two packs silently disagreeing would make their beliefs unmergeable -- with the symptom appearing nowhere near the cause.

grounding.why:
The hole the validator leaves. `the old mill by the river` in a world with no mill contains no proper noun and no number, so a capitalisation rule passes it -- and a character asserting the existence of something that does not exist is exactly what makes a language model untrustworthy in an NPC's mouth.

The head of the phrase is what is flagged, not the adjective: `the old mill` asserts a mill, not an `old`. One agent deliberately answers to `anchor` and `the bar`, which a PLACE already claims: the index keeps the FIRST claim, so a later character cannot steal a name an earlier room answers to. And a world's own multi-word names are indexed word by word, because `The Harbour Front` being a place makes `harbour` this world's vocabulary -- without that, every world's own nouns read as inventions the moment they appear alone.

sentences.text: I saw her at the old mill by the river.
She was at the clinic that night.
He came through the door and stood by the window.
A courier dropped a package near the gantry.
Nothing happened in the city months ago.
The old mill was mentioned in the plan.
That is his crowbar long, not mine.
I went to The Anchor and then to the harbourfront.
She mentioned the surgery and a strange contraption.

expresses.text: I have no idea what you mean.
Byrne was down at the harbour.

flat.why: The representation most shipped games actually use, implemented honestly and sitting in the repository next to the thing it is compared against. It is not stupid: it is fast, it saves and loads, every designer understands it, and it has shipped a thousand games. The comparison is never `flags are bad` -- it is a list of questions and which of the two can ANSWER them, and every `None` here is a structural fact about booleans rather than an opinion about anyone's craft.

tuning.why:
One block names its engines OUT of alphabetical order, because `apply` sorts them and a block already in order cannot show it. One refusal misspells a parameter as `w_`, which is a prefix of five of memory's names -- the only place the `did you mean` list is longer than the three it keeps.

A tuning value silently ignored because it was misspelled is the worst failure this module could have: the world behaves as though nothing was set, the author believes it was, and the gap between them is invisible.

This case also does something no other case does: it compares the PORT'S OWN PARAMETER TABLE against Python's live dictionaries, name by name and value by value. Python reads `engine.params` and gets the names for free; C++ has no reflection, so they are written out by hand -- and a hand-written copy of somebody else's field list is exactly the thing that drifts. A parameter added to an engine and forgotten here would become a knob that silently does nothing, which is the failure this module exists to prevent.

revision.why:
Lowering trust in a liar changes what they will manage to convince you of NEXT time and does nothing about what they already did -- which is the part that matters, because the whole point of exposing somebody is that the things they told you stop counting.

The floor is 0.1 and not zero: people who lie about one thing were sometimes telling the truth about another, and erasing everything they said would make exposing them strictly better than never having heard them. And a belief with an independent source keeps it: being caught in one lie does not make everything you ever said false. A rumour three hops away still names the liar, because the ORIGIN survives retelling even though the speaker does not.

pursuit.why:
Diffusion is who happens to talk; pursuit is who has a REASON to. The same act -- one character asserting something to another -- chosen by a different question. Relevance comes before conviction: somebody trying not to be arrested raises the thing that bears on being arrested, not the thing they happen to be surest about.

The phone is a FALLBACK and not a preference: ranking every contact in the world against the room turned five days into ninety-eight phone calls and thirty-four conversations, which is not a market square. And somebody alone in a room used to be skipped outright, which was right while pursuit could only speak and exactly wrong once it can write.

goals.content: warn my sister about the dock

pursuit.why:
Each of these exists because a mutation survived without it.

The world starts at time ZERO, where the default `last acted` of -10^9 is not merely `long ago` -- it is what makes everybody due on the first tick rather than nobody. Somebody stands ALONE in a room, which is the note case and the only one the old guard skipped. One goal has priority 0.5, so its interval is six hours rather than three and a flat interval cannot be told from a scaled one. Two possible listeners are trusted EXACTLY equally, so the tie-break on the lower id decides. One remote contact is trusted 0.40 against 0.35 in the room -- above it, but not by the 0.12 that makes a phone call worth it. And one belief has more keywords in common with the goal than any other while sitting just BELOW the confidence floor, which is the only shape in which relevance-before-conviction and the floor itself can be told apart -- on a predicate the CATALOGUE DOES NOT KNOW, because a catalogued predicate takes its slot names from the schema and an invented slot never reaches the key at all.

goals.content: the flood and the clinic and the dock

pursuit.why: With media off there is nothing to ring, so everybody outside the room is equally out of reach -- which is exactly when a note stops being a curiosity and becomes the only way to reach anyone. Also: with the layer itself off, nothing is scheduled and nothing is emitted.
Off means the tick is exactly what it was: diffusion is who happens to talk, and nobody has a reason to do anything.

notes.why:
A note is not a slower phone call: a conversation is gone the moment it ends and a note is still there, which makes it the runtime's first piece of EVIDENCE rather than testimony -- a claim with an author attached that the author cannot take back.

The recipient stays AWAY for most of the run, which is the only way anything is ever intercepted -- an earlier version had them walk in and read both notes on the first step, so the interception path, the curiosity weighting, the per-note cap and the hours floor were all dead. Notes sit in three places declared out of alphabetical order, one step is shorter than an hour, and the author stands over his own note the whole time.

Three paths the first case cannot reach. An author standing ALONE over his own note, because the guard against reading what you wrote yourself only matters when nobody else is there to read it first. Twenty occupants in one hall, declared in REVERSE alphabetical order -- because ids are unique, so any correct sort agrees, and only a cast whose declaration order differs from its sorted order can show the sort doing anything at all. Many short steps, because the hours floor rounds anything under an hour UP to one and a single sixty-minute step sits exactly on it. And eight notes in a closet watched by somebody with no curiosity at all, who almost never notices one in a short step -- so they are still lying there unread at the hundred-hour step, where the raw chance reaches 1.0 and the cap of 0.6 is the only thing standing between a stranger and every letter in the room.
Off means `leave` returns false and writes nothing, so a caller can ask unconditionally and a world without the layer is exactly the world before it.

promises.why:
Not against the truth: this runtime holds no ground truth about whether somebody paid, and inventing an oracle here would contradict the whole design. A promise is kept when the promisee comes to BELIEVE it was -- so one quietly fulfilled where they never find out damages the promiser exactly as much as one that was broken, which is unfair, true, and the reason people make a point of being seen to deliver.

The margin is a MOVEMENT and not an absolute. One first-hand confirmation moves a belief from 0.500 to 0.537, so a fixed 0.55 silently required two independent confirmations before anybody was credited with keeping a promise made to them personally. The believer here moves from 0.500 to exactly 0.537 -- kept on the movement, BROKEN on any absolute threshold of 0.55 and broken on a margin of 0.05, which is the only place those three answers part company. Another promisee already believes it at 0.700 and never moves: broken on the movement, kept on an absolute threshold, and kept again if the prior were assumed to be 0.5. And one promise names its recipient with `addressee` rather than `target`, because both spellings are accepted and only one was ever used.

settle_explicitly.note: the game handed over the money

promises.why: Off means no promise is recorded and none resolves -- so a run reproduces exactly what it did before this layer existed.

common_knowledge.why:
Two events land on exactly two people -- one speaker plus one listener, and two listeners with no speaker -- because three is the smallest crowd that is not a conversation, and a threshold nothing sits on cannot be told from a lower one. Two people talking already know that they both know; Chwe's argument is about an audience.

Publicity is not evidence and this module does not touch belief. What it changes is what can be DONE: a scandal everyone privately knows is deniable, and the moment it is common knowledge denying it stops working. Two separate public moments about the same fact produce TWO publics, not one merged crowd -- somebody in the square on Tuesday does not thereby know about the people in the bar on Wednesday -- but a larger crowd absorbs a smaller one it contains, because that would be counting one moment twice.
Off means the crowds are never recorded and never asked about -- not a smaller effect, none.

climate.why:
One event carries an `importance` of 0.93 rather than 0.5, because the fallback IS 0.5 -- an event whose importance happens to equal the default cannot show that the field is read at all. And walks are run again AFTER the steps, because the per-step carry budget is cleared on a step and a run that never crosses that boundary cannot see it cleared.

Weather, not personality. A killing in the square makes the square quieter and a stranger asking questions trusted less, and nobody's traits moved. The baseline is derived from what packs ALREADY declare -- a gossipy market is candid, a surveilled place guarded, a private room closed -- so an existing world gets a sensible climate without anybody authoring one, and an authored `climate` block wins outright.

Off returns the neutral modifier set -- a tempo of exactly 1.0 and three zeroes -- so a caller applies them without knowing this module exists and the arithmetic is identical to a world where it never ran.

contagion.why:
One exchange is between the two most opposite moods the runtime allows, heard by somebody with no emotional stability who knows and likes the speaker completely -- the only configuration in which the per-exchange cap of 0.22 actually binds. Every other pairing here moves less than that, so without it the cap is untested.

A chain of exchanges, so the accumulation is visible rather than one step of it. Damped by the listener's emotional stability -- which is what that trait is FOR, and using it here means it does work instead of sitting in a character sheet -- and weighted by how much they care about the speaker, because a stranger's bad afternoon is not catching.
Off means the transfer never happens, not a smaller one. Every optional layer in this runtime is asserted byte-identical when off rather than promised to be.

medium.why: Who can reach whom is half the layer. A room is who is standing in it; a phone is who has your number, authored or inferred from familiarity -- and the inference is a DEFAULT, not a finding, which is why a pack that declares contacts overrides it entirely. With the layer off every exchange is face to face or does not happen, which is exactly what it was before.

agency.why:
One character carries the SAME identity id as the caller under a different group, because `shared_group` compares the concrete group and not the label -- two people can both be `id:crew` in different crews, and that is not a shared circle. Twelve more are reachable but barely, so the summed expectation runs over fifteen values rather than three: a compensated sum and a naive one agree for two addends and can part company beyond that.

Calling for backup is an ACTION whose payoff is the summed chance each ally answers -- loyalty, kinship weighted by urgency, a favour owed, authority, minus what it costs a disagreeable person to turn up. Standing gates REACH: an officer answers only somebody with the standing to call one, which is why the same cry for help reaches different people depending on who is shouting.

dialogue.why:
A second speaker holds four beliefs clustered at 0.62, 0.61, 0.59 and 0.58, straddling the 0.6 assertion threshold -- because with the threshold lowered the two extra candidates fall inside the equal-enough band of the best and the seeded pick changes. The first speaker's beliefs are far apart, so lowering the threshold there adds candidates that could never win and changes nothing.

A plan carries the avoid LABEL of a secret and never its content, so a secret cannot leak by sitting in a prompt. Only four acts assert anything -- everything else commits to no fact and hands the text layer nothing to choose from -- and a belief below 0.6, or one a secret protects, never becomes a candidate however confident the character is.

factions.why: Clocks fill and heat decays over ten steps of world time. One clock is one segment from done and one is ALREADY done, because `tick` returns true only on the tick that completes it -- a clock at full that draws again must announce nothing, and a clock that merely reaches full in the middle of the run never draws again to prove it; one faction has influence 0.77, so its mobilise latency is 14.6 and Python truncates it to 14 where a rounding port says 15; and two factions differ in resources with four goals between them, because the rate is influence TIMES resources and a single goal over five steps cannot tell them apart, seeded per faction and per clock -- so `derive_seed` is called with a CLOCK NAME where the signature says event id, which is legal in Python and needs an overload in C++. Influence scales both how fast a faction gets things done and how quickly it answers, which is the point of the layer.

commitment.why:
One case has two candidates whose scores differ only in the SIXTH decimal, because the sort key is the ROUNDED value: they rank as equal and the proposition's own text breaks the tie, where a port sorting on the raw doubles would order them by noise. My first attempt used 0.99991 and 0.99999, which round to different fourth decimals and proved nothing.

The decision a text provider used to make. A spoken claim is a real event that moves other characters' beliefs, so letting a model pick which facts reach the listener means the model decides what enters the society -- and the claim that the text layer only phrases things was untrue. Everything within a small band of the best score is treated as equally good and chosen by SEED, which gives the same unpredictability from the player's side and stays in the event log.

sociolinguistics.why:
A grid over the politeness thresholds, and one speaker per shape against six listeners in four rooms. The grid exists because the four politeness strategies are chosen by four comparisons -- `> 0.7`, `< 0.5`, `< 0.3`, `> 0.6`, `< 0.4` -- and a style vector produced by the full pipeline lands ON one of those boundaries essentially never, so the boundary is untested by anything else here. One speaker is a gang member in a formal room, whose slang comes out between 0 and 0.2: the only band where the lexicon threshold decides anything.

Accommodation is a DIAL and not a switch, which is the fix this module carries a scar from: `1 if liking >= 0 else -1` was a cliff at exactly zero, so a stranger got the full pull toward the other's register and one small unkindness later got the full push away -- formality 0.568 to 0.097 on a fifteen-hundredth of a unit. The listeners here sit at 0.0, a hair either side of it, and well past 0.5 where the dial saturates.

social_status with an observer is perceived status, and it has claimed to be appearance-mediated since the day it was written while consulting reputation only. With no reactions the appearance term is exactly zero and it returns what it always did -- which is why adding it changed no shipped pack.

standing.why: The whole claim of this layer. The same cruelty judged at five confidences by four observers who care about the victim to different degrees -- somebody who watched it, somebody who was told, somebody who barely credits it. What you saw yourself weighs more than what you heard because CERTAINTY scales the delta, not a hop count somebody tuned.
With the layer off no judgement is made at all -- not a smaller one. Off being byte-identical is what lets this ship disabled, and it is asserted rather than promised.

`standing_conduct` is merged, not replaced: adding `stole_from` must not silently delete the two the demo relies on, and retuning `helped` must keep its dimension unless the pack says otherwise. A partial spec -- weight only -- inherits the rest.

warmth reads three things that are three different things -- affection, whether your word is worth anything, and what they think of your conduct toward OTHER people -- and `decent` carries half, because it is the one a bystander has. influence deliberately excludes liking. And the bias is what makes any of it matter: before it, standing moved and nothing read it when deciding what to say.

appearance.why:
Status and threat are two numbers because gang colours are not low-status, they are something else entirely. Sensitivity scales both, and 0.0 is somebody who genuinely does not care what you are wearing. With no reactions authored -- which is every shipped pack -- every read is empty and nothing changes, which is why this is authored data rather than a layer with a flag.

One subject sums to NEGATIVE threat, because status is bipolar and threat is not: being read as harmless is the absence of threat, not its negative, and only a negative total can tell the two clamps apart. And the bias is asked about every action in the catalogue rather than only those aimed at the subject, because a check that is never given a mismatched target proves nothing.

diffusion.why:
The whole path at once: who talks to whom, whether they would pass THIS to THIS person here, what the retelling becomes, who overhears, and what the claim event carries. Every seeded draw in it happens inside a loop over a collection -- speaker, listener, topic, topology gate, distortion, bystanders, stifling -- which is seven chances to walk a container differently and get a different town.

Four beliefs deliberately score IDENTICALLY, declared out of alphabetical order. `_tellable` sorts by score descending and then by the proposition key ascending, and the second key only decides anything on a tie -- so without one the ranking looks correct while resting on insertion order.

Two guards. A delta of zero is not a window and must produce nothing. And forty people in one gossipy room over four hours goes past max_encounters_per_tick, which has to defer rather than run quadratic -- the cap is the reason a crowded scene is affordable at all.

content.why:
Content is where a pack's own vocabulary lives, and every one of these has a truthiness fallback a port gets wrong: an empty label falls back to the id, an empty avoid_label falls back to `protected_topic`, an empty template resolves to nothing rather than to itself. The alias index is longest-first for a reason -- `police post` must beat `police`, or `go police post` walks you to an officer.

Two details are here because they were invisible without them. Three aliases of EQUAL length in non-alphabetical order, because the sort's second key only decides anything on a tie. And an avoid_label that sorts BEFORE the ones declared earlier, because `avoid_labels` de-duplicates in first-appearance order and the previous labels happened to already be alphabetical -- so a port that sorted them looked identical.

secrets.summary: her brother is hiding at the clinic

cover_phrasings.neutral: He was down at the dock.

distortion.why:
Levelling, sharpening, assimilation and inversion, each forced by its own weights so all four paths are exercised rather than whichever the seed happened to pick. Allport & Postman: most of what is lost in a retelling is simply lost, and inversion is rare -- which is why the old coin-flip model was wrong.

Three of the details here exist because an earlier version of this case could not see them. An amount of 7 sharpens to 10.5, where Python's int() truncates to 10 and a rounded port would say 11 -- 300 grows to exactly 450 and hides the difference. A slot holding 0 alongside one holding 7 shows that `str(value or "")` treats zero as absent, which a lone zero cannot, because 0 times 1.5 is 0 and the claim is unchanged either way. And five familiar agents, not two, because the list is capped at three.

A character must not leak a secret by accidentally distorting a different claim into it. The protected key here is exactly what levelling would produce, so the first candidate is rejected and the next process is tried -- which is the only reason the fallback loop exists.

A one-slot claim has no droppable detail, no quantity and no agent the teller could confuse -- so levelling, sharpening and assimilation all decline, and only inversion is left. A port that returned the unchanged proposition instead of nothing would have a character solemnly retell a claim as itself.

social.why: The tie strength diffusion selects on, and the bridge score that raises it for people whose role puts them where circles cross. Also every value-term provider at once, because they all write into the same policy groups and a port that swapped two group names would still produce plausible numbers. One context sits EXACTLY on the front-stage threshold of 0.3, because a boundary nobody lands on cannot tell > from >= -- and an earlier version of this case, with 0.8, 0.0 and 0.31, could not.

routine.why: Four characters on overlapping schedules. Exercises the wrap past midnight -- before the first block of the day somebody is still in the LAST block of the previous one, which is what lets an author write an overnight shift once instead of twice. The fourth step advances the clock to 22:00 with delta 0 while a move IS due: nothing may happen, because a window of no time is not a window. The last step skips seven days at once and must land everyone correctly WITHOUT emitting a week of arrivals.

Python sorts the blocks with `sorted`, which is stable, and block_at keeps the LAST block whose start is at or before now -- so blocks declared for the same minute resolve to the one written last. TWENTY of them, not three: libstdc++ falls back to insertion sort below sixteen elements and insertion sort is stable, so a small case passes std::sort and proves nothing. This is the third time that has bitten in this port.

meeting_opportunities is the authoring aid that answers whether a pack can produce a rumour at all. A cast whose schedules never coincide returns nothing, and that has to be visible before playtesting rather than after -- two of three reference packs were in this state and the benchmark reported SKIP.

perception.why: Six people in one place, one of them the actor. Everybody else gets a seeded jitter -- so this is the first case where a seeded draw happens INSIDE a loop over a collection, which is the exact shape a port gets wrong. occupants() sorts by id for that reason; without it the same event is heard differently by different people in each implementation. The last two events MOVE somebody first, because the occupancy index is cached and a cache that is never invalidated passes every case where nobody walks -- which was true of an earlier version of this one.

A broadcast ignores the room entirely and asks who was tuned in. `if exposure:` is a truthiness test, so an empty record is not an audience -- a port testing for the key would have somebody hear a radio they had switched off.

Quality is clamped at zero, not allowed to go negative. At noise 1.0 the base term vanishes and only the jitter is left -- so half the room hears nothing at all and the other half barely, which is what a clamp on the wrong side would hide.

topology.why: Not slowly -- at all. A claim declared `access: [role:engineer]` returns exactly 0.0 to anybody outside, which is one of the only two categorical zeroes in this module. Every other brake is a tendency, because people do leak restricted things and a model where they never do is not a model of people. Also covers two things a pack can do that the table does not anticipate: invent a classification name (which falls back to 0.85, not to 1.0 -- an earlier version of this case never reached that branch and passed a port that got it wrong), and override the weight outright.

A claim that only circulates in two places returns 0.0 anywhere else -- the second categorical zero. And shop talk is scaled by the LISTENER's competence, so the same claim between the same two people is worth different amounts depending on which of them is listening.

int(round(x)) rounds HALF TO EVEN in Python: curiosity 0.5833... puts the budget on 6.5, and the answer is 6, not 7. std::round would give 7 and nothing downstream would ever point at the comparator. Also exercises the day boundary, which uses floor division.

affect.why: Desirability and praiseworthiness together, from another's agency: joy, admiration and gratitude all fire, in that order, and the impulses are summed in it.
The truthiness trap. prior_fear is PRESENT and zero, so `if appraisal.get('prior_fear')` is false and no relief fires. A port testing for the key produces an emotion out of nothing.

Six strong hits in a row. Mood must approach the rail asymptotically, never reach it: the impulse is scaled by (1 - |mood|), so one enormous event cannot slam a character to +/-1 and leave them there.
Anger at one person is not anger at the room. Two targets, then enough time for one to fall below epsilon and be dropped while the other survives.

relationship.why: Four kindnesses and one betrayal, all in one batch. Positive and negative are summed separately and applied at 0.10 and 0.40, so the character does not end up where they started. A port that averaged them would make trust cheap to rebuild.

fear, respect, dependence and trust are clamped to [0,1] -- there is no negative fear here, only its absence -- while liking and any authored field are bipolar and may go to -1. Every delta here is large and NEGATIVE on purpose: pushing them up hits 1.0 under either clamp, so a case that only pushes up cannot tell the two apart. This one caught a deliberately mis-clamped respect that an earlier version of it did not.
Three subjects interleaved. The groups come out in first-appearance order, and each sum is a floating-point addition in arrival order -- sorting either would change the last bit.
Reputation is per audience AND per dimension, and a missing dimension falls back to 'general'. Bipolar, clamped, applied at full amount rather than through a gain.

identity.why: Two rounds. The first has no previous distribution and is a plain softmax; the second blends half of it back in, which is what stops a character switching who they are between two sentences.
Two identities with identical everything. Python's max keeps the FIRST maximum in iteration order, so the winner is the one the pack listed first -- not whichever hashed lowest.
Nothing is salient. Without the absolute neutral baseline a softmax always elects a winner however weak the field, and a character would always be strongly something.

policy.why: The bug this channel exists to prevent. A +0.12 push toward evading, contributed as a TERM into a safety group already holding +0.24, lowers it -- somebody dressed to look dangerous makes a character LESS likely to back away. Here the same push arrives as a bias and raises the utility. Both channels are exercised at once so a port that merged them fails on the direction, not the magnitude.

`if pushed:` -- a bias of exactly 0.0 contributes nothing AND no line in the breakdown. A port using `is not None` adds a row that changes the explanation without changing the number, which is worse than either.

A high temperature and four close candidates: the sampled action is often NOT the top-rated one, and which one it is comes from derive_seed and seeded_choice. This is where a port with a correct utility function and a wrong seed silently produces a different character.

The optional transform, which applies to OUTCOMES and not to arbitrary terms. The speculative job has a big upside at middling probability -- exactly the shape prospect weighting bends, and the case that would pass unnoticed with the flag ignored.

A temperature of 0.001 with a calm, conscientious character. Without the max(0.05, ...) floor the softmax over utilities overflows exp() and the choice becomes greedy -- a character who is never surprising again. No other case here reaches the floor, and an earlier version of this file passed a port that had removed it.

Forty affordances with identical utility. Which one a character does is decided entirely by sort stability and then by the seed. FORTY because libstdc++ falls back to insertion sort below sixteen elements and insertion sort is stable, so the six-action reference catalogue passes a deliberately unstable comparator -- a studio's own catalogue would not.
Ten terms in one group. Averaging keeps it in [-1,1]; summing would put the group at 4.0 and drown every other consideration -- which is what bounded_aggregate is for.

memory.why: Same type, same single presentation, importance 0.05 against 0.95. Importance must slow the DECAY, not add a bonus: the gap has to widen with time, not stay constant.

Forty memories with identical everything. Every activation ties, so the order out must be the order in, and only the first seven survive the working-memory cap -- so the answer is literally which memory the character brings up. FORTY, not six: libstdc++ falls back to insertion sort below sixteen elements and insertion sort is stable, so a small case passes a deliberately unstable comparator. An earlier version of this case had six and did exactly that.

Thirty episodes of equal importance and equal activation against a cap of five. Which twenty-five are destroyed is decided entirely by sort stability, and nothing else in the run would ever point at the comparator.

A memory below threshold comes back anyway when something in the scene points at it -- that is what `a > tau_ret - 1.0` is for. The relevance path also exercises the ontology's slot matching from inside the memory engine.

Twelve episodes over the cap, nine of them about the same person doing the same thing. The episodes are evicted and a judgement is drawn out of them first -- otherwise a character can live through the same thing fifty times and conclude nothing. The judgement keeps pointers to the five strongest.
Forty recalls against a window of thirty-two. The oldest timestamps go and the newest are kept, because old presentations contribute dt^-d and are negligible beside recent ones.

interpretation.note: One hull seal fails in Stores, and five people are in the room. The engineer identifies it; the tourist cannot and ends up holding a coarser claim; the person the claim NAMES attends to it hardest; a curious neighbour attends because she knows him; and an incurious one in poor light never notices at all -- which is a different state from disbelief. The same event told over the radio skips recognition entirely, because a stated claim has already been identified by whoever stated it. `hull_breached` carries an EMPTY competence declaration, which Python reads as no declaration at all rather than as a level of zero. Five further observers exist only to land ON a boundary: competence exactly at the professional-interest gate, exactly at the recognition threshold once the slack is subtracted, one step inside that slack, a curiosity that differs from neutral by less than the epsilon the engine ignores, and an attention score that comes out exactly at the floor -- which takes a NEGATIVE importance, because importance is not clamped and the boundary is worth probing whatever a sane pack would author.

parser.note: Every branch of the parser, and every place two vocabularies can collide. The world's topic is called `market_attack`, which is the bug this design exists for: `ask honce about the market attack` contains the word 'attack' and used to be parsed as an assault, so the topic could not be raised at all -- by anyone, ever, in that world. A LEADING verb now decides, and the contains-anywhere pass stays as the fallback for 'i want to threaten him'. `news` is likewise both a radio word and part of a topic alias. `help` is the command list and `help byrne` is a kindness, which only works because every `assist` word keeps its trailing space. Umlauts fold, so `gehe zur TUER` and `gehe zur tür` are the same line. And `wait 0` extracts a zero, which Python reads as falsy -- so it waits half an hour rather than no time at all. `place:tuer` is labelled with an umlaut and authors no alias, so the index files it under `tür` while the parser normalises the line to `tuer` -- the room is unreachable. That is a finding about the engine, not about the port, and it is reproduced rather than repaired: a place a player cannot walk to is worth seeing in the fixture. Two NPCs share the market, so a line that names nobody resolves to nobody rather than to whoever happens to be first -- and the player is excluded by their CONFIGURED id, which is why a line that is just the word `player` addresses no one. The garment table is read in SORTED order and not insertion order, which `wear the worn coat over the apron` is there to prove, and `_default` is skipped, which `wear the default jacket` is there to prove.

parser.note: A pack may replace an intent's whole word list, and nothing stops it authoring an EMPTY word. `"".startswith` is true of every string, so an empty word would make its intent match every line typed. Two guards keep that from happening and both are load-bearing: the leading-verb pass drops words that are nothing but whitespace, and an alias of `""` is filtered out of the alias index. The contains-anywhere fallback has NO such guard -- `"" in low` is true -- so an empty word still swallows every line that gets that far, which is what this case records rather than hides.

validator.note: The last thing that runs before a line reaches a player. Every layer, and every way each one can be wrong. A secret leaks by ALIAS and not only by its label, which is why the surface forms are pack vocabulary. A number, an invented name and a real name the speaker was not licensed to use are three different findings and are reported as three different kinds. A sentence-initial capital is usually grammar and is skipped -- unless the world knows the word, because `Kane told me.` is never grammar. The grounding pass adds `the old mill by the river`, which has no capital and no number and would otherwise pass; a token that trips BOTH rules is reported once. `warn` releases what `strict` rejects. And the repetition window is a Python slice, so a window of zero is the WHOLE history rather than none of it -- which is the opposite of what the name suggests. A boat is also called Byrne, and a character already answers to that name: the term table keeps the FIRST claim, so an entity cannot take a name a character answers to. `the Mill` trips both rules at once -- capitalised and invented -- and is reported once. `Please` and `Thanks` are capitalised in the middle of a sentence and carry no reference, and a single capital `A` is too short to be a name. The single capital is `Z` and not `A` for a reason worth writing down: the licence test is a SUBSTRING test, and every plan here licenses an `agent:...` id, so the letter `a` is licensed by accident and the too-short-to-be-a-name guard could never be seen to do anything.

actionbridge.note: Issue, resolve, expire, snapshot, reload. Two intents are issued in the SAME world minute, so the pending order has to be broken by the id and not by whatever the map happens to hold; one is resolved, one is left to time out. A result is reported in lower case, because an engine over HTTP will. A second result for one intent is refused, and so is a status outside the closed set and a type outside the closed catalogue -- all three as errors, because none of them is a state this runtime can hold. TIMED_OUT is counted like any other outcome: a build quietly timing out every intent must not look identical to a build with no bridge attached. The pending order is probed three ways: two intents in the SAME minute inserted in the opposite order to their ids, and one issued for a later minute inserted before one issued for an earlier. And the expiry boundary is checked on the minute itself, which does NOT expire, as well as one minute later, which does. A reloaded tally carries a status this build has never heard of, and it is dropped rather than counted.

provider.note: The deterministic realizer, and the clean-up that decides what a chatty local model is allowed to have said. Register is picked at both thresholds and on them. A pack overrides ONE variant of one act and inherits the other two. An act with no template at all falls back to a deflection and records that the commitment did NOT reach the words -- which matters because what is committed becomes a world event, and a character silently deflecting to the player while the society heard them assert something is two different conversations. An authored phrasing with an EMPTY neutral variant still counts as authored, because `a or b` returns b however falsy b is, and that single difference decides whether the fallback runs. Slang substitution keeps the tail of the original word at the KEY's length, so a word with leading punctuation loses it -- reproduced rather than tidied. Four of the seven scaffolding markers are DEAD and the cases say so rather than pretending otherwise: the markdown strip removes underscores before the marker scan runs, so `dialogue_act`, `avoid_topics`, `allowed_facts` and `max_length` have already become `dialogueact` and friends by the time anything looks for them. Only `addressee`, `agent:` and `{` can still fire. That is a finding about the engine, reproduced rather than repaired -- a port that quietly fixed it would release text the reference build rejects, and refuse text it accepts.

runtime.note: The whole loop, driven and then compared field by field: every belief with its provenance, every memory, every mood, every relationship, the world clock, the event watermark, the scheduled queue and the reason trace. An attack is WITNESSED, so it is believed on evidence and not on how far the victim trusts their assailant. A question names a claim without asserting it. A character hearing themselves speak learns nothing. One observer distrusts the radio specifically and another distrusts radio in general, and only the most specific match is charged. Two keepers share a belonging, so an attack on one alarms the other. Then a week is advanced in eight steps with every optional layer switched ON, which is the case that proves the tick ORDER: routines move people before diffusion decides who is standing next to whom, and diffusion runs before consolidation enforces the memory cap. Two claims are SCHEDULED into one time advance and both reach the same listeners, which is the only way to tell an accumulating trace bucket from a replacing one. The radio speaker is himself exposed to the channel he speaks on -- the one path in the engine on which a character can perceive their own utterance, and therefore the only place the you-learn-nothing-from-hearing-yourself guard is reachable at all. And a third keeper stands in the market when one of them is attacked, because the victim's own alarm is handled elsewhere and the layer is about the people watching. The last advance is a full week, because a threatened belonging halves every day and only stops being carried at all once it falls under a hundredth -- seven half-lives away from where an attack leaves it. A run that stops before then cannot tell fading from forgetting. The tail runs with population LOD ON, which is where a dormant character stops being decayed every tick and is caught up lazily instead. A fresh attack raises a belonging threat, a week passes with nobody looking at her, and only when she next perceives something does the catch-up run -- which is the moment the threat, now under a hundredth, stops being carried at all. A run that never touches a dormant agent again cannot tell an exact deferred decay from no decay. A dozen further claims arrive inside two ticks so the working-memory cap is actually reached -- without them consolidation is configured and never runs, and a port that skipped it entirely would pass. And a promise is made in front of witnesses and then comes due, which is the only thing that makes the promise ledger's place in the tick order observable. Two hundred and ten further claims land in one tick, because the episodic memory cap is two hundred and a run that never reaches it cannot tell a runtime that consolidates from one that does not. The market is authored as a public place and the bar as a private one, which is what decides whether anything said there becomes common knowledge. A claim about CONDUCT -- `mistreated(by=..., who=...)`, and those two slot names are the whole interface: no `by`, no judgement -- is the only kind the standing layer has an opinion about. And two characters carry goals that name the seal, so one of them has a reason to go and raise it with the other, and to leave word when they are not there. The same claim about conduct is made TWICE -- once before the standing layer is switched on and once after -- because off has to be provably off, and a case where every conduct claim arrives after the switch cannot show it. Pursuit's note-writing is switched on with the rest, so somebody who can reach nobody writes it down instead. The session ends by exporting itself, letting the world run on for ten more hours, and putting the export back -- which has to land on exactly the state the export was taken from, down to every provenance chain and every decay watermark. Then the same capture is put back eleven times, each with one thing wrong with it: no schema version, an older one, a different seed, a character this pack does not define, a character the save predates, no decay watermarks, no event watermark, a faction nobody has heard of. Every one of those is survivable and every one has to be REPORTED, because a load that lost something quietly is worse than one that refused. The cast is authored out of alphabetical order on purpose: the fingerprint sorts it and so does the missing-agent report, and neither can be seen to do so in a world whose characters were listed alphabetically to begin with. Finally the inspector prints all five characters, character for character. That is a stricter comparison than it sounds: a reason detail is rendered as a Python DICT, so the two implementations have to agree on what a float, a string and a None look like inside one -- and on a character with no memories, no beliefs and no trace, which prints three different kinds of nothing. The inspector runs three times: before anything has happened, when nobody believes or remembers or feels anything and three different kinds of nothing have to be printed; immediately after an assault, when several emotions are live at once and the action-tendency list is longer than the five it shows; and at the end.

snapshot.note: The refusal paths, and the one that is deliberately NOT a refusal. A patch that adds or retires a character must not invalidate a save, so a fingerprint mismatch is reported and loaded through; a save with no overlap at all is somebody else's game and is refused. The envelope and the payload carry separate versions because a loader wants to fail differently at each: an unreadable envelope is 'this is not our file' and an unreadable payload is 'this save is from a newer build'. The SHA-256 vectors are here because the fingerprint is one, and a hash that differed between the two builds would reject every cross-build save.

inspect.note: The inspector, driven directly rather than through a session, so the awkward cases can be authored instead of waited for. A character whose only live emotion is fear has THREE action tendencies of equal magnitude -- hide, seek_safety and attack -- which is what tells a stable sort from an unstable one; a run of the simulation never happened to produce a tie. A trace detail carries floats at both ends of Python's notation rule (1e15 prints in full and 1e16 does not, 0.0001 does and 1e-05 does not), a nested dict, a tuple, a one-element tuple with its trailing comma, None, True, and a string containing both kinds of quote. One character feels all ten emotions at once, which produces twenty-three action tendencies with ties among them. That number matters: libstdc++ falls back to insertion sort below sixteen elements and insertion sort is stable, so a shorter list cannot tell `std::sort` from `std::stable_sort` -- the same trap that hid an unstable memory retrieval earlier in this port. Every emotion is at full intensity, so several tendencies saturate at exactly 1.0 and the tie is at the TOP of the list -- where a five-entry slice can still see it.

pack_loader.note: All six shipped world packs, loaded by both implementations and compared field by field -- places, entities, channels, topics, the whole cast with its personality, education, secrets and routine, the media exposures, the factions, the scheduled events with the ids the LOADER gave them, and the predicate catalogue the pack registered. This is the first case that reads the packs a game actually ships rather than a scenario written for the probe, and it is what makes `usc conformance --check --port` possible at all. The character list is passed in rather than discovered: listing a directory is the one thing a console does differently, and the host is the right place to answer it. One further pack declares almost nothing, and it is here because the six shipped ones declare everything: without it the loader's defaults -- the seed, the clock, the player's starting room, an event with no time of its own, an exposure with no attention, a `_note` sitting in a table read as data, a character file with no personality at all -- were all unreachable, and every one of them could have been wrong. And one more whose scenario names a clock, so an event that gives no time of its own can be seen to inherit the SCENARIO time rather than zero -- which the bare pack cannot show, its clock being zero.

sdk.note: The five conformance scenarios, played end to end by BOTH implementations against the same shipped packs: a player types, the parser maps it, the world moves, a character answers, and the whole mutable state is exported and compared field by field -- every belief with its provenance chain, every memory, every mood, every relationship, every promise, every reason. This is the case the port exists for. The player-facing MESSAGE is compared too, which the conformance format deliberately does not require: a port is free to phrase it differently, and this one is not free, because the same sentence coming out of both is the cheapest possible evidence that the same thing happened inside. Three further runs exist because the five fixtures, between them, never reach eleven of the branches this module has: a room with more than three bystanders, a character with two sayable facts rather than one, a topic asked a third time, a protected proposition that would otherwise be sayable, a belief sitting between the two confidence floors, a target who is not in the room, and a secret that has become common knowledge. They run with every optional layer switched on, which is also the configuration no shipped fixture uses.
